text:
6.8 Integrated regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
Sensitivity analysis integrated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency




Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",

)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

nrow(data_complete_cases)

6.11 Identified regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
Sensitivity analysis identified_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency

#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed

6.14 Introjected regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
Sensitivity analysis introjected_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency




Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item)

#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

6.17 External regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA
Sensitivity analysis external_regulation_SMS2 and BEA, time latency




Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)

[1] 121

  "SMS_2_15_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

external_regulation_SMS2_thetas <- RIestThetas(external_regulation_SMS2_validity_analyses)

data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE
data_complete_cases$external_regulation_SMS2_thetas_WLE <- external_regulation_SMS2_thetas$WLE

6.20 Amotivated regulation (SMS-2) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between amotivated_regulation_SMS2 and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.

Preparing item data frames

#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed

title: 7  Competitive State Anxiety Inventory-2 Revised (CSAI-2R)
text:
7.1 Competitive State Anxiety Inventory-2 Revised (CSAI-2R) and BEA validity analysis
Competitive State Anxiety Inventory-2 Revised (CSAI-2R) is used as part of the validity investigation of BEA. CSAI-2R consists of 17 items and three sub-scales divided into the following according to Cox et al. (2003) and Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005): Cognitive anxiety sub-scale (items 7, 10, 13, 16, 22); Somatic anxiety sub-scale (items 5, 8, 11, 17, 20, 23, 26); Self-confidence sub-scale (items 9, 15, 18, 24, 27). Note that the original item numbers from CSAI-2 are used. These three sub-scales of CSAI-2R will be used and analyzed separate with Rasch analysis. Validity analyses by correlations of thetas between BEA and each respective CSAI-2R sub-scale will then be undertaken. Lastly, partial correlations were conducted to examine the association between BEA and CSAI-2R sub-scales, while controlling for the shared variance among the sub-scales. Note that CSAI-2R was not completed by the participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien), therefore more missing values than in the BEA Rasch analysis are to be expected.

  filter(`Instansens namn` == "Vecka 1") %>%
  distinct(`Användarnamn`, .keep_all = TRUE)

merged_data_hockeystudien_BE <- full_join(sheet1_filtered, sheet2_filtered, by = "Användarnamn")

#hockeystudien demographics
hockeystudien_intervention_demographics <- read_excel("hockeystudien intervention_demographics.xlsx", sheet = 1)

#corecting age for a participant in the df
hockeystudien_intervention_demographics$Demografi.Alder[hockeystudien_intervention_demographics$Användarnamn == "1077dhrv" &
                                                          hockeystudien_intervention_demographics$Demografi.Alder == 6] <- 26


#merge df BE and demographics from hockeystudien
merged_data_hockeystudien_BE_demographics <- full_join(merged_data_hockeystudien_BE,
                                                       hockeystudien_intervention_demographics,
                                                       by = "Användarnamn")

#following in the hockeystudien study already exists in the bulls eye study, therefore mask:
#mask 1029spns, 1061bgmb, 1043gsnq, 1046pkbz, 1062xhqd, 1070mfqq
#1073znwk is also masked due to not completing the dart board ratings in BEA (only other parts of BEA) and therefore not contributing with any values for the statistical analyses

usernames_to_exclude <- c("1029spns",
                          "1061bgmb",
                          "1043gsnq",
                          "1046pkbz",
                          "1062xhqd",
                          "1070mfqq",
                          "1073znwk")

filtered_data <- merged_data_hockeystudien_BE_demographics %>%
  filter(!(`Användarnamn` %in% usernames_to_exclude))


hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(`Användarnamn` = paste0(`Användarnamn`, "_hockeystudien")) %>%  # Append "_hockeystudien" to each value
  rename(
    BE_Competition = Tavling,
    BE_Training = Traning,
    BE_PreparationRecovery = Forberedelser,
    BE_Life = Livet,
    BE_Obstacles_Sport = HinderSkala1,
    BE_Obstacles_Life = HinderSkala2
  )




#preparations for merging datasets into superfinal version (bulls eye + hockeystudien_bulls eye)

hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data <- hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data %>%
  mutate(from_hockeystudien = 1)

BullsEye_merged_data_final <- BullsEye_merged_data_final %>%
  mutate(from_hockeystudien = 0)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bind_rows(hockeystudien_bulls_eye_modified_data,
                                              BullsEye_merged_data_final) #use for analyses

#BE items (dartboard), adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
BE_adjust <- c(
  "BE_Competition",
  "BE_Training",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "BE_Competition_test2",
  "BE_Training_test2",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery_test2",
  "BE_Life_test2"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, BE_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, BE_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#"Hinder", reverse items (low value = low in values-based living and compatible with other values items) and adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
Hinder_reverse_and_adjust <- c(
  "BE_Obstacles_Sport",
  "BE_Obstacles_Life",
  "BE_Obstacles_Sport_test2",
  "BE_Obstacles_Life_test2"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, Hinder_reverse_and_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, Hinder_reverse_and_adjust], function(x)
  8 - x - 1)

#ADAQ, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
ADAQ_adjust <- c("ADAQ.1",
                 "ADAQ.2",
                 "ADAQ.3",
                 "ADAQ.4",
                 "ADAQ.5",
                 "ADAQ.6",
                 "ADAQ.7")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, ADAQ_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, ADAQ_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#SWLS, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
SWLS_adjust <- c("SWLS.1", "SWLS.2", "SWLS.3", "SWLS.4", "SWLS.5")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SWLS_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SWLS_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#VQ adjustments
#some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform, but no items should be reversed in VQ when using each subscale separately. Some items were therefore reversed back.
#items 1, 2, 6, 8, 10 (the VQ obstruction subscale) were reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back.
#VQ already starts at zero and does therefore not need to be adjusted prior to Rasch analysis.

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(c("VQ.1", "VQ.2", "VQ.6", "VQ.8", "VQ.10"), ~ 6 - .))

#SMS-2 adjustments
#SMS-2 consists of 18 items and 6 sub-scales divided into the following according to Pelletier et al. (2013). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform, but no items should be reversed in SMS-2. Some items were therefore reversed back.
#Intrinsic regulation: items 3, 9, 17 (none reversed = correct)
#Integrated regulation: items 4, 11, 14 (none reversed = correct) 
#Identified regulation: items 6, 12, 18 (none reversed = correct)
#Introjected regulation: items 1, 7, 16 (items 1 and 7 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#External regulation: items 5, 8, 15 (items 5 and 8 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#Amotivated regulation: 2, 10, 13 (items 2, 10 and 13 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)

#(back) reverse scoring for items 1, 7, 5, 8, 2, 10, 13
SMS2_items_to_reverse <- c("SMS_2_1", "SMS_2_7", "SMS_2_5", 
                      "SMS_2_8", "SMS_2_2", "SMS_2_10", "SMS_2_13")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(SMS2_items_to_reverse), ~ 8 - .))

#SMS-2, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
SMS2_adjust <- c("SMS_2_1",
                 "SMS_2_2",
                 "SMS_2_3",
                 "SMS_2_4",
                 "SMS_2_5",
                 "SMS_2_6",
                 "SMS_2_7",
                 "SMS_2_8",
                 "SMS_2_9",
                 "SMS_2_10",
                 "SMS_2_11",
                 "SMS_2_12",
                 "SMS_2_13",
                 "SMS_2_14",
                 "SMS_2_15",
                 "SMS_2_16",
                 "SMS_2_17",
                 "SMS_2_18"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SMS2_adjust] <- lapply(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, SMS2_adjust], function(x)
  x - 1)

#CSAI-2R adjustments
#CSAI-2R consists of 17 items and 3 sub-scales divided into the following according to Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Items will be renamed so they correspond to item numbers in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform (self-confidence sub-scale items), but no items needs to be reversed in CSAI-2R when looking at each sub-scale separately. Items in the self-confidence sub-scale were therefore reversed back.
#items in brackets are the original item numbers found in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005), items prior to brackets were the item numbers used on the web platform used for data collection in this study
#cognitive anxiety sub-scale: items 2 (7), 5 (10), 7 (13), 9 (16), 13 (22)
#somatic anxiety sub-scale: items 1 (5), 3 (8), 6 (11), 10 (17), 12 (20), 14 (23), 16 (26)
#self-confidence sub-scale: items 4 (9), 8 (15), 11 (18), 15 (24), 17 (27) 

#rename CSAI-2R item names to correspond with Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005):
item_mapping_CSAI2R <- c(
  "CSAI_2R_1" = "CSAI_2R_5",
  "CSAI_2R_2" = "CSAI_2R_7",
  "CSAI_2R_3" = "CSAI_2R_8",
  "CSAI_2R_4" = "CSAI_2R_9",
  "CSAI_2R_5" = "CSAI_2R_10",
  "CSAI_2R_6" = "CSAI_2R_11",
  "CSAI_2R_7" = "CSAI_2R_13",
  "CSAI_2R_8" = "CSAI_2R_15",
  "CSAI_2R_9" = "CSAI_2R_16",
  "CSAI_2R_10" = "CSAI_2R_17",
  "CSAI_2R_11" = "CSAI_2R_18",
  "CSAI_2R_12" = "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_13" = "CSAI_2R_22",
  "CSAI_2R_14" = "CSAI_2R_23",
  "CSAI_2R_15" = "CSAI_2R_24",
  "CSAI_2R_16" = "CSAI_2R_26",
  "CSAI_2R_17" = "CSAI_2R_27"
)

names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data) <- sapply(
  names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data),
  function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(item_mapping_CSAI2R), item_mapping_CSAI2R[x], x)
)

#(back) reverse scoring for self-confidence sub-scale items 9, 15, 18, 24, 27
CSAI2R_items_to_reverse <- c("CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_15", "CSAI_2R_18", "CSAI_2R_24", "CSAI_2R_27")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(CSAI2R_items_to_reverse), ~ 5 - .))

#CSAI-2R, adjust (-1) to enable Rasch analysis
CSAI2R_adjust <- c(
  "CSAI_2R_5", "CSAI_2R_7", "CSAI_2R_8", "CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_10", "CSAI_2R_11",
  "CSAI_2R_13", "CSAI_2R_15", "CSAI_2R_16", "CSAI_2R_17", "CSAI_2R_18", "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_22", "CSAI_2R_23", "CSAI_2R_24", "CSAI_2R_26", "CSAI_2R_27"
)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, CSAI2R_adjust] <- lapply(
  bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, CSAI2R_adjust],
  function(x) x - 1
)

#adding recoded bulls eye items (from the BEA Rasch analysis, needed here as the loading of data needs to be repeated for each quarto file)
recode <- dplyr::recode

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Recoding BE_Competition (0+1; 2+3; 4+5)
    BE_Competition_recoded = recode(
      BE_Competition,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1, `3` = 1,
      `4` = 2, `5` = 2,
      `6` = 3
    ),
    # Recoding BE_Training (0+1)
    BE_Training_recoded = recode(
      BE_Training,
      `0` = 0, `1` = 0,
      `2` = 1,
      `3` = 2, 
      `4` = 3,
      `5` = 4,
      `6` = 5
    ))

7.5 Cognitive anxiety (CSAI-2R) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between cognitive_anxiety_CSAI2R and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation cognitive_anxiety_CSAI2R and BEA
Sensitivity analysis cognitive_anxiety_CSAI2R and BEA, time latency




Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)

[1] 121





Code#item data frames

)]

  "CSAI_2R_22"
)]

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 
data_complete_cases$cognitive_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_WLE <- cognitive_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas$WLE

7.7 Re-analysis of somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R recoded version
Based on the analysis of the response categories and threshold locations, scale steps were merged and recoded so that each kept scale step had the highest response probability at some point on the person location scale, and also so that all threshold locations were in the right order for all items. Recoded items were given new names with the abbreviation “_recoded”.

7.9 Somatic anxiety (CSAI-2R) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R and BEA
Sensitivity analysis somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R and BEA, time latency




Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)

[1] 121





Code#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "CSAI_2R_5_recoded",
  "CSAI_2R_8",
  "CSAI_2R_11_revised",
  "CSAI_2R_17",
  "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_23_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas <- RIestThetas(somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 
data_complete_cases$somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_WLE <- somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas$WLE




Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

Code{
  plot(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE,
       main = "Index Plot of BE_thetas_WLE",
       ylab = "BE Theta",
       xlab = "Participant Index",
       pch = 20)
  abline(h = mean(data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE), col = "blue", lty = 2)
  points(28, data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE[28], col = "red", pch = 19)
}










Code#participant on row 28 is an outlier and therefore removed
correlation_BE_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases[-28, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_WLE",
  y = "somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R)

------------------------------
BE_thetas_WLE |  -1.05 | 0.296

Observations: 120

Codeplot(correlation_BE_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R)









Some participants did not complete BEA and CSAI-2R during the same day as intended. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis is conducted.

Code#creating data frame with only participants that completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day
#since 17 participants did not (has already been checked in a prior validity analysis), 104 participants will remain 
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day <- subset(data_complete_cases, time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1)



Code#looking only at participants who completed Bulls Eye and the other scales during the same day (N = 104)

#sensitivity analysis somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R and BE
BE_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_validity_analyses_less1day <- data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[, c(
  "CSAI_2R_5_recoded",
  "CSAI_2R_8",
  "CSAI_2R_11_revised",
  "CSAI_2R_17",
  "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_23_recoded"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses_less1day)

somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_less1day <- RIestThetas(somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_validity_analyses_less1day)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$BE_thetas_less1day_WLE <- BE_thetas_less1day$WLE

data_complete_cases_less_than_1day$somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_less1day_WLE <- somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_less1day$WLE

#analysis only with participants completing Bulls Eye and CSAI-2R the same day
#removing the outlier, now on row 20 in the data frame
correlation_BE_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_less1day <- cor_test(
  data_complete_cases_less_than_1day[-20, ],
  x = "BE_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  y = "somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_less1day_WLE",
  method = "pearson"
)

print(correlation_BE_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_less1day)

Parameter1             |                                 Parameter2 |     r
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

-------------------------------------------------------
BE_thetas_less1day_WLE | [-0.31, 0.07] |  -1.31 | 0.195

Observations: 103



Code#we can also check if there is a statistically significant difference 
#by adding same or different day as a predictor 
#the outlier on row 28 in the data frame is removed
data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

m0_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R <- lm(somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

m1_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R <- lm(somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R_thetas_WLE ~ BE_thetas_WLE + group, data = data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis[-28, ])

anova(m0_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R, m1_somatic_anxiety_CSAI2R)

7.12 Self-confidence (CSAI-2R) and BEA validity analysis
Validity between self_confidence_CSAI2R and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. As both scales has undergone Rasch analysis, participants theta estimates (computed with weighted likelihood estimation - WLE) will be correlated, and since thetas are interval data, Pearson’s correlation is applied.


Prepring data
Preparing item data frames
Outlier identification
Correlation self_confidence_CSAI2R and BEA
Sensitivity analysis self_confidence_CSAI2R and BEA, time latency




Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)

[1] 121





Code#item data frames
BE_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

self_confidence_CSAI2R_validity_analyses <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "CSAI_2R_9",
  "CSAI_2R_15",
  "CSAI_2R_18",
  "CSAI_2R_27"
)]

#extracting thetas
BE_thetas <- RIestThetas(BE_validity_analyses)

self_confidence_CSAI2R_thetas <- RIestThetas(self_confidence_CSAI2R_validity_analyses)

#adding thetas to the data frame
data_complete_cases$BE_thetas_WLE <- BE_thetas$WLE 
data_complete_cases$self_confidence_CSAI2R_thetas_WLE <- self_confidence_CSAI2R_thetas$WLE




Visual inspection of potential outliers was only conducted for BEA to have the same sub-sample across validity correlation analyses. One statistical outlier was detected and marked in red in the plot below. This participant was row 28 in the data frame and will be removed in the upcoming correlation.

data_complete_cases_sensitivity_analysis <- data_complete_cases %>% 
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(time_latency_survey1_bulls_eye1_days < 1,"same_day","different_day")))

#Intrinsic regulation: items 3, 9, 17 (none reversed = correct)
#Integrated regulation: items 4, 11, 14 (none reversed = correct) 
#Identified regulation: items 6, 12, 18 (none reversed = correct)
#Introjected regulation: items 1, 7, 16 (items 1 and 7 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#External regulation: items 5, 8, 15 (items 5 and 8 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)
#Amotivated regulation: 2, 10, 13 (items 2, 10 and 13 are reversed in the scoring and needs to be reversed back)

#CSAI-2R adjustments

Items will be renamed so they correspond to item numbers in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005). Some items were reversed in the scoring when exporting data from the web platform (self-confidence sub-scale items), but no items needs to be reversed in CSAI-2R when looking at each sub-scale separately. Items in the self-confidence sub-scale were therefore reversed back.
#items in brackets are the original item numbers found in Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005), items prior to brackets were the item numbers used on the web platform used for data collection in this study
#cognitive anxiety sub-scale: items 2 (7), 5 (10), 7 (13), 9 (16), 13 (22)
#somatic anxiety sub-scale: items 1 (5), 3 (8), 6 (11), 10 (17), 12 (20), 14 (23), 16 (26)
#self-confidence sub-scale: items 4 (9), 8 (15), 11 (18), 15 (24), 17 (27) 

#rename CSAI-2R item names to correspond with Lundqvist & Hassmén (2005):
item_mapping_CSAI2R <- c(
  "CSAI_2R_1" = "CSAI_2R_5",
  "CSAI_2R_2" = "CSAI_2R_7",
  "CSAI_2R_3" = "CSAI_2R_8",
  "CSAI_2R_4" = "CSAI_2R_9",
  "CSAI_2R_5" = "CSAI_2R_10",

  "CSAI_2R_7" = "CSAI_2R_13",
  "CSAI_2R_8" = "CSAI_2R_15",
  "CSAI_2R_9" = "CSAI_2R_16",
  "CSAI_2R_10" = "CSAI_2R_17",
  "CSAI_2R_11" = "CSAI_2R_18",
  "CSAI_2R_12" = "CSAI_2R_20",
  "CSAI_2R_13" = "CSAI_2R_22",
  "CSAI_2R_14" = "CSAI_2R_23",
  "CSAI_2R_15" = "CSAI_2R_24",

)

names(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data) <- sapply(

  function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(item_mapping_CSAI2R), item_mapping_CSAI2R[x], x)
)

#(back) reverse scoring for self-confidence sub-scale items 9, 15, 18, 24, 27
CSAI2R_items_to_reverse <- c("CSAI_2R_9", "CSAI_2R_15", "CSAI_2R_18", "CSAI_2R_24", "CSAI_2R_27")

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%

)

)

bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data %>%

    BE_Competition_recoded = recode(

    BE_Training_recoded = recode(

title: 8  Subjective performance rating
section: 8.2 Subjective performance rating and BEA validity analysis
text:
8.2 Subjective performance rating and BEA validity analysis
Validity between the subjective performance rating and BEA is investigated by correlation analysis. The subjective performance rating has not undergone Rasch analysis (since it is only one item), thus participants ordinal scores will be correlated. Since it is ordinal data, Spearman’s rank correlation is applied.

Codeitemlabels <- data.frame(itemnr = c("item1"),
                         item = c("During the last week, my athletic performance has been: 1 (“Extremely poor”) to 10 (“Extremely good”)"))


RIlistitems(itemlabels, all.items = TRUE)

Item data frame preparations and plot of ordinal scores

Code#complete cases data frame for validity analyses

#removing missing values in relevant items for complete cases analysis
#only BE items and one item from the other scales in the bulls eye study
#is needed (in this case the SubjektivPrestation item) 
#this is because there are no missing values for the other scales 
#after the intervention study (Hockeystudien) participants have been removed
#therefore this data frame will work for all validity analyses 

items_validity_analyses <- c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life",
  "SubjektivPrestation"
)

data_complete_cases <- bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[complete.cases(bulls_eye_merged_superfinal_data[, items_validity_analyses]), ]

#155 participants to begin with
#33 participants from the intervention study (Hockeystudien) were removed (did not complete any scale beside Bulls Eye)
#1 participant (not from the intervention study) who completed the other scales but not the dartboard in Bulls Eye (only other parts of BE) and were therefore removed
#results in a complete cases data frame with 121 participants 

nrow(data_complete_cases)

[1] 121





Code#item preparation and plot of ordinal scores
performance_rating <- data_complete_cases[, c("SubjektivPrestation")]

BE_items <- data_complete_cases[, c(
  "BE_Competition_recoded",
  "BE_Training_recoded",
  "BE_PreparationRecovery",
  "BE_Life"
)]

BE_items_names <- names(BE_items)
performance_rating_names <- names(performance_rating)

#computing ordinal scores 
data_complete_cases_performance_rating_BE <- data_complete_cases %>%
  mutate(
    performance_rating_sum = rowSums(select(., all_of(
      performance_rating_names
    )), na.rm = TRUE),
    BE_sum = rowSums(select(., all_of(BE_items_names)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

#plot of ordinal scores (raw data, not ranked)
ggplot(data_complete_cases_performance_rating_BE, aes(x = performance_rating_sum, y = BE_sum)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Scatterplot of Performance rating vs BE Sum Scores",
    x = "Performance rating",
    y = "BE Sum Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()










Code#compute Spearman's rank correlation
#participant on row 28 identified as outlier in previous validity analyses and therefore removed to have the same sub-sample across analyses
correlation_performance_rating_BE <- correlation(data_complete_cases_performance_rating_BE[-28, c("performance_rating_sum", "BE_sum")], method = "spearman")

print(correlation_performance_rating_BE)

# Correlation Matrix (spearman-method)

Parameter1             | Parameter2 |  rho |       95% CI |        S |         p
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
performance_rating_sum |     BE_sum | 0.31 | [0.14, 0.47] | 1.98e+05 | < .001***

p-value adjustment method: Holm (1979)
Observations: 120




Some participants did not complete BEA and the subjective performance rating during the same day as intended. Therefore, a sensitivity analysis is conducted.

  mutate(
    performance_rating_sum = rowSums(select(

Result from sensitivity analysis correlation is close to the original correlation.
